name: Florida DMV Permit Test

issuer.name: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV)

trademarkNotice: This practice resource is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles. The agency's name is used only to identify the test this material helps you prepare for.

examInfo.format: 50 multiple choice questions on Florida traffic laws, safe driving practices, and traffic controls such as signs and signals. The exam is taken at a driver license office or, for applicants under 18, online through an approved third party administrator. FLHSMV describes its exam as a timed 60-minute test. This practice mock uses 4 answer choices per question.

passCriteria.description: You must answer at least 40 of the 50 questions correctly (80%).

content.eligibility: You can apply for a Florida learner's license at age 15. First-time drivers must complete a Driver Education Traffic Safety (DETS) course, pass vision and hearing tests, and pass the Class E Knowledge Exam. Applicants under 18 also need a signed parental consent form. Check the FLHSMV website for the current documents and fees before you go.
content.intro: The Florida permit test (officially the Class E Knowledge Exam) checks that you know Florida traffic laws and road signs before you get a learner's license or a first Florida driver license. It has 50 multiple choice questions on traffic laws, safe driving practices, and traffic controls, and you need at least 40 correct answers (80%) to pass. The questions are based on the Florida Driver License Handbook. Practicing short sets every day helps you remember the numbers and rules that are easy to mix up.
content.trendSummary: The exam covers both road signs and road rules. Sign shapes and colors, flashing signals, right-of-way at four-way stops and when turning left, Florida speed limits, parking distances, school bus stops, the Move Over law, and alcohol, phone, and teen driver laws are the topics new drivers most often need to review. The chapters on this site are study groupings, not official test sections.
content.studyTip: Start with Beginner sets on signs and right of way, then add the chapters with numbers (speed limits, parking distances, signaling distance, blood alcohol limits). Put every missed question in your review notes and redo them the next day. The passing mark is high (80%), so before test day take a full 50-question Mock Exam and aim for at least 43 correct to leave a safety margin.

faqs.question: What score do I need to pass the Florida permit test?
faqs.answer: You need at least 40 correct answers out of 50 questions, which is 80%.

faqs.question: Can I take the knowledge exam online?
faqs.answer: Applicants under 18 can take the Class E Knowledge Exam online through an approved third party administrator. Online tests need a parent proctoring form. Check the FLHSMV website for the current rules before you sign up.

faqs.question: Are these the real Florida test questions?
faqs.answer: No. Every question here is an original practice question written from the rules in the Florida Driver License Handbook and Florida law. The actual test questions are not public, so use this site to learn the rules and read the official handbook as well.

faqs.question: What language is the exam in?
faqs.answer: Since February 2026, Florida gives the Class E Knowledge Exam in English only. The driver handbook is still published in other languages for study. Check the FLHSMV website for the latest rules before your appointment.

studyTips.studyOrder: Start with Signs, Signals, and Pavement Markings, then Right of Way and Turns. These two chapters teach the basic rules that the other three build on. Next study Speed, Passing, and Parking, then Safe Driving and Sharing the Road, and finish with Licensing, Alcohol, and Driver Responsibility. Each chapter carries the same weight in our practice sets, so do not skip any of them.
studyTips.hardChapters: Speed, Passing, and Parking is full of numbers that are easy to mix up, such as 30 and 55 mph default limits, 100 feet for signaling, and the 15, 20, 30, and 50 foot parking distances, so keep them in one list. Safe Driving and Sharing the Road has the school bus and Move Over rules, where small details like a raised median or 20 mph below the limit decide the answer. Licensing, Alcohol, and Driver Responsibility depends on exact teen driving hours and blood alcohol limits.
studyTips.examDay: You need 40 correct answers out of 50 (80%), so you can miss no more than 10 questions. Read every answer choice before you pick one, because wrong choices often differ by a single number or word. If a question is hard, think about which choice keeps pedestrians and other drivers safest.
